does: Dusts a piece of food, often after it has been marinated, in a thin layer of potato starch or cornstarch just before frying. It fries to a crisp, light, pale crust.
how: Pat the food dry and shake off any marinade that is dripping.
Tip the starch into a tray and turn each piece in it, pressing lightly.
Tap off the loose starch, as too much turns pasty in the oil.
Fry straight away, before the starch dampens and turns gluey.

cues.text: The coating is thin, dry and even, with no wet spots.
The piece crackles in the oil.

mistakes.mistake: Coating too thickly, which turns gluey and heavy.
Coating long before frying, so that the starch gets wet.

variant_of.differs: The coat is starch, not flour, so it fries thinner, crisper and paler.
